scenarioStory.history: G2P1 at 38 weeks gestation presents with regular contractions 2 minutes apart for the last hour and a strong urge to push. Prenatal ultrasound at 36 weeks noted breech presentation; external cephalic version was scheduled but labor began before the appointment. Membranes ruptured 30 minutes ago with clear fluid. Patient reports feeling something firm and rounded at the vaginal opening, not the baby's head.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 26-year-old G2P1 female at 38 weeks with complete breech presentation — buttocks and both feet visible at the vaginal opening — with strong contractions and an uncontrollable urge to push. → Buttocks and trunk delivered hands-off: The buttocks, feet, and trunk deliver spontaneously with the mother's own pushing effort. Crew supports the body without pulling, checks for a prolapsed cord, and prepares to assist head delivery. → Head delivered with jaw-flexion support: The head fails to deliver spontaneously after a brief pause, so the crew inserts a gloved hand to flex the fetal neck and create an airway, then completes delivery of the head. → Newborn dried, warmed, and stabilized: The newborn is delivered completely, dried, warmed, and stimulated with good cry and color. Cord is clamped after 1 minute; APGAR is scored; mother and newborn are packaged for transport.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 26-year-old G2P1 female at 38 weeks with complete breech presentation — buttocks and both feet visible at the vaginal opening — with strong contractions and an uncontrollable urge to push.
relatedChecklist: Allow buttocks, feet, and trunk to deliver spontaneously without traction
Assess for prolapsed cord after trunk delivers
Support fetal body without traction; keep fetus elevated off the umbilical cord

scenarioEvents.name: Buttocks and trunk delivered hands-off
scenarioEvents.description: The buttocks, feet, and trunk deliver spontaneously with the mother's own pushing effort. Crew supports the body without pulling, checks for a prolapsed cord, and prepares to assist head delivery.
relatedChecklist: Insert gloved hand, form a V with index/ring fingers on fetal cheeks to flex chin to chest and open airway
Do not routinely suction the newborn's airway, even with a bulb syringe

scenarioEvents.name: Head delivered with jaw-flexion support
scenarioEvents.description: The head fails to deliver spontaneously after a brief pause, so the crew inserts a gloved hand to flex the fetal neck and create an airway, then completes delivery of the head.
relatedChecklist: Dry, warm, and stimulate newborn; place skin-to-skin on maternal chest
Clamp cord ~5-6 inches from abdomen after a 1-minute delay, then cut between clamps
Record APGAR score at 1 and 5 minutes once neonate is stabilized

scenarioEvents.name: Newborn dried, warmed, and stabilized
scenarioEvents.description: The newborn is delivered completely, dried, warmed, and stimulated with good cry and color. Cord is clamped after 1 minute; APGAR is scored; mother and newborn are packaged for transport.

scenarioEvents.name: Traction applied to speed delivery
scenarioEvents.description: Instead of allowing the breech to deliver hands-off, the crew pulls on the fetal trunk to hasten delivery. This extends the arms above the head (nuchal arm entrapment), obstructing further delivery and risking cervical spine injury and fetal hypoxia.
relatedChecklist: Recognize obstructed delivery from traction; rotate fetal trunk to free the extended arm(s), then resume hands-off support

checklist.title: Allow buttocks, feet, and trunk to deliver spontaneously without traction
Assess for prolapsed cord after trunk delivers
Support fetal body without traction; keep fetus elevated off the umbilical cord
Insert gloved hand, form a V with index/ring fingers on fetal cheeks to flex chin to chest and open airway
Do not routinely suction the newborn's airway, even with a bulb syringe
Dry, warm, and stimulate newborn; place skin-to-skin on maternal chest
Clamp cord ~5-6 inches from abdomen after a 1-minute delay, then cut between clamps
Record APGAR score at 1 and 5 minutes once neonate is stabilized
Recognize obstructed delivery from traction; rotate fetal trunk to free the extended arm(s), then resume hands-off support
